subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why does the UK import a large share of its food?
options: The UK has banned domestic farming
Imported food is always cheaper to grow
The UK grows none of its own food
Demand for variety and out-of-season produce exceeds what the UK climate can grow
questions.explain: The UK imports food to meet year-round demand for variety and produce that its climate cannot grow, even though it produces much of its own.

questions.q: Desalination increases water supply but its main drawback is that it:
options: Is expensive and uses large amounts of energy
questions.explain: Desalination provides fresh water from seawater but is costly and energy-intensive, raising costs and emissions.

questions.q: What does 'water security' mean?
options: Reliable access to enough safe, affordable water
Having more rivers than neighbouring countries
questions.explain: Water security is the reliable availability of an adequate, safe and affordable supply of water to meet a population's needs.

questions.q: A reservoir created by a dam is used to:
options: Store water and often generate hydroelectricity
questions.explain: Dams hold back water in reservoirs to provide a reliable supply and often to generate hydroelectric power.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is naturally replenished, whereas coal, gas and uranium are finite and cannot be renewed on a human timescale.

questions.q: Globally, demand for food, water and energy is rising mainly because of:
options: Population growth and rising living standards
questions.explain: A growing global population combined with higher incomes and consumption increases demand for all three resources.

questions.q: Which farming approach is most sustainable?
options: Permaculture and organic methods that protect the soil
questions.explain: Permaculture and organic farming maintain soil health and biodiversity, making food production more sustainable.

questions.q: One environmental impact of extracting fossil fuels is:
questions.explain: Resource extraction such as mining and drilling can pollute land and water and damage ecosystems.

questions.q: A 'water deficit' region is one where:
options: Rainfall is very high all year
There are no rivers at all
Demand for water is greater than the supply available
questions.explain: A water deficit occurs where demand exceeds available supply, typically in densely populated or drier regions.

questions.q: An advantage of solar power compared with coal is that it:
options: Is cheaper to run in every location
Produces no carbon dioxide when generating electricity
questions.explain: Solar panels generate electricity without burning fuel, producing no CO2 during operation, though output varies with sunshine.

questions.q: Which method increases food supply but can cause salinisation of soils?
questions.explain: Heavy irrigation in hot dry areas can draw salts to the surface as water evaporates, leading to salinisation that damages soils.

questions.q: An advantage of nuclear power over fossil fuels is that it:
options: Produces very little carbon dioxide when generating electricity
questions.explain: Nuclear power emits very little CO2 during generation, though it produces radioactive waste and uses a finite fuel.

questions.q: The UK's energy mix has changed in recent years by:
options: Increasing the share of renewables and gas while reducing coal
questions.explain: The UK has cut coal use sharply and increased the contribution of renewables (especially wind) and natural gas.

questions.q: A major physical cause of water scarcity is:
options: Low rainfall combined with high evaporation
questions.explain: Low and unreliable rainfall together with high evaporation in hot climates reduces available water and causes physical scarcity.

questions.q: Which of these best shows global inequality in food consumption?
options: Many people in HICs over-consume while millions in LICs are undernourished
Everyone eats roughly the same number of calories
LICs consume more calories per person than HICs
Food is shared equally between all countries
questions.explain: Food consumption is highly unequal, with over-consumption and obesity in many richer countries while undernutrition persists in poorer ones.

questions.q: Which is the best example of sustainable water management?
options: Extracting groundwater faster than it refills
questions.explain: Cutting leaks and reusing grey water reduces demand and conserves supply, making them sustainable strategies.

questions.q: Which statement about renewable energy is correct?
options: It never has any environmental impact
It is the same as nuclear power
It always produces more electricity than fossil fuels
It is naturally replenished and will not run out
questions.explain: Renewable energy comes from sources that are naturally replenished, such as wind and sunlight, so they are not depleted.

questions.q: Why might a country face 'economic' water scarcity despite having water?
options: It has banned the use of water
It lacks the money or infrastructure to supply it
questions.explain: Economic water scarcity occurs where water exists but a lack of investment and infrastructure prevents people accessing it.

questions.q: Which is a non-renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Crude oil is a finite fossil fuel that cannot be replenished on a human timescale, unlike solar, geothermal and tidal energy.

questions.q: Compared with HICs, many LICs typically have:
options: No use of energy at all
questions.explain: People in lower-income countries generally consume far less energy per person than those in high-income countries.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a water transfer scheme?
options: To move water from areas of surplus to areas of deficit
questions.explain: Water transfer schemes move water from regions with a surplus to regions with a deficit to balance supply and demand.

questions.q: Fracking (hydraulic fracturing) is used to extract:
options: Shale gas and oil from rock
questions.explain: Fracking pumps high-pressure fluid into rock to release trapped shale gas and oil, but raises concerns about pollution and earth tremors.
